bench.prompt: Create a new original horizontal landscape 3:2 painting for this adventure game's inspectable work surfaces. Use references for convincing tactile painterly rendering and the rough hut, not for exact composition. An intimate eye-level/slightly downward still life inside Epigwaitt, a handmade castaways' hut in the subantarctic Auckland Islands in 1865; an extreme close shot of ONE sole continuous hand-hewn pine plank workbench beneath an uneven plank wall. Visible brushwork and granular drybrush highlights on worn edges and soft pigment washes in the shadows; period maritime oil study with indigo and umber shadows, pale oatmeal and muted golden ochre accents, cold left window light from just out of frame and a warmer reflection on the cloth. Raking light follows the grain of the broad plank. Simple asymmetrical three-group composition, painterly negative spaces, right angles and organic torn fabric. At x 24%, y 43%, a small unmistakable blunt naked wooden peg projecting horizontally from the back timber toward us; enough room to hang cloth below it. At x 77%, y 42% a SINGLE short thick rough removable loose slanting board rests against an upright with a generous dark wedge-shaped open cubby BELOW IT at x 76% y 57% easily bright enough to see and place something. These left/right landmarks empty, on same work surface, separated by clear space. Near front center (x 50%, y 75%) a small partly unrolled OATMEAL linen tool fold holding a tiny hand wrapped hank of golden waxed sailmaker's thread and one conspicuous plain steel sail needle, a folded 12 cm square of sailcloth for a patch, ONE faint woven blue selvedge stripe on sailcloth for recognizability. Thrifty field repairs. Those are the only loose things; clear zones at peg and beneath sloping board. Cropped in close, tactile homely signs of work; entire painting fills the frame, no mounts, no annotation, no captions, no text, no UI, no people, no ocean vista, nothing modern. Both peg and sheltered space and the central fold need crisp silhouettes even on phone. Paint a completed original work, no diagram and no multi-panel.

ending.prompt: Paint an original cinematic horizontal 3:2, approximately 1.6:1, oil and gouache narrative vignette for the last page of the Grafton shipwreck story, Carnley Harbour, Auckland Island, August 1865. A long parting look from within the now unoccupied rough hut Epigwaitt, through its simple OPEN doorway out across a silvery subantarctic inlet. Foreground left: two empty bunk ends with two brown blankets folded down, a few little domestic scuffs on the threshold, modest hearth stones now cold. Only two sleeping places implied, not five men. A little rubbed light catches the rail of one bunk. The spare dark cinder-brown interior frames middle-right water, where far from shore a tiny single-masted cutter Flying Scud, unmistakable cream triangular sail, is beginning to leave; no tall ship, no steamer, no visible identifiable people. Beyond, low round near-black landforms, wind-clipped rata to one side, streaks of late winter cloud, pale late light glimpsed in ash-violet banks, thin gold band of reflection in slate blue sea. Make the boat and open door the visual payoff. This is an evocative imagined closing image, not a literal reconstruction or spatial diagram, and must be a single immersive painting (no montage). Painterly original work with bristle strokes indicating distance, warm/cool colour counterpoint, thoughtful rather than triumphant, tangible maritime material work. Use reference images only for the spirit of the light and the spare hut. No snow-capped pinnacles, no typography, no date, no frame, no logos, no HUD, no portrait. Weight of visual descriptions above should read clearly in a 400px wide card.
